Indian Standard
METHOD OF . MILK RECORDING OF CATTLE
0. FOREWORD

`

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 November 1972, after the draft finalized by the Animal Housing and Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Capacity for milk production is one of the criteria for assessing the genetic qualities of cattle. This capacity is assessed from. systematic records of the amount of milk produced and of one or more of the quality characteristics of the milk, that is, butterfat content, solids-non-fat, protein The obtaining of these data, their recording and their content, etc. rational utilization, to assess the capacity for milk production- of herd of cattle, constitutes what is known as milk recording. 0.3 Milk recording fulfils a *two-fold purpose: a) at the level of the individual breeder, it provides an objective means of selection of the females under test, based on the quantity and quality of their milk, and permits a more efficient management of the herd, technically and economically; and b) at the collective level, it contributes to the characterization of a given breed, to the determination of the value of a sire, and to research activities generally on questions related to genetics and economics. 0;4 The milk recording carried out by either: practices described by or in this standard should be

Method A -That is, exclusively controlling authority;

qualified

staff attached

to the

Method B -That is, by the owner of the cattle or his representative, in collaboration with the controlling authority. However, the analysis of the milk should be effected only by the controlling authority. 0.5 The form in which milk recording data are presented, and their interpretation, demand a rigorous standardization of the various operations 3

assigned to the recorders. Standardization of the general organization of the control work to meet the animal husbandry requirements and those associated with the mechanical processing of the data in question should be desirable. 0.6 Finally, the standardization stock on a well organized basis. is required especially for selling breed

0.7 This standard should be applied widely in the country for indicating the capacity of milk production of milch cattle on a scientific basis and better assessment of collective yields of large *herds. This standard is applicable to milch cattle of normal lactation period. On the basis of this method, data on milch cattle having lactation period of less than 305 days will be screened in respect of differ,e,nt breeds of indigenous milch cattle. Consequently, this standard might be aniended or supplemented. 0.8 In the preparation of this sfandard, considerable assistance has been derived from ISO/R 1546 Method of milk recording of cows issued by the International Organization for Standardization. 0.9 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a `test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance `The number of significant places retained in the with IS : 2 - 1960*. rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard describes the method of milk recording which should be adopted for all cattle of dairy breed or of breeds with a predominant milk capacity in any one herd.
1.2 This standard production. concerns, however, only to milk production and fat

2. TERMINOLOGY

2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply.
2.1 Cattle type. NOTE Cross breds with exotic breeds may also be considered as milch type.

The term cattle shall include COWS and buffaloes of milch `

-*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised). 4

2.2 Herd - A herd is a group of cattle kept for the same purpose, belonging to thd same owner, and accommodated in the same group of farm buildings. 3. GENERAL PRINCIPLE

3.1 Determination of the total milk and butterfat production of the cattle during her successive lactations or operational years throughout her life, from the data obtained at selected time intervals, without any correction or modification, for the quantity of milk and of fat produced over 24 hour periods. 4. RECORDING STAFF be carried out dy specially qualified and

4.1 Milk recording should suitably trained personnel. 5. TECHNIQUE

dF MILK RECORDING

5.1 Duration - Each periodical milk recording operation should extend over a period of 24 hours; an exhaustive milking should be carried out \ every time that it is felt necessary.
NOTE - Milking carried out at the normal time interval immediately preceding The results of the milkings which are the subject of the daily recording in question. Should, however, this milking are noted but not normally included in the calculation. the results of a daily milking be mislaid or lost, it is preferable rather than to discard the recording, to use the results of the exhaustive milking in the& place in the calculation.

5.2 Determination of the Quantjty of Milk Prod&d - By means of a weighing mach,ine graduated in units of not more than 200 g, which is approved by the authorities responsible for supervising the milk recording practices and tested periodically, determine the mass of milk collected at the usual milking times from the cattle under_ test, during 24 hours. Express the result in kilogrammes, to one decimal place, 5.3 Determination of Butterfat Content

5.3.1 Constitution of the Sam$eAt each milking, draw a sample after complete mixing of the milk. The size of these primary samples should be proportional to the quantity of milk obtained at each of these milkings, except in the case of milkings carried out at approximately equal time intervals, when samples may be of equal size. Mix the primary samples well and render homogeneous the average sample thus obtained. 5.3.2 Keeping of the Samples -It is important that thdmilk be kept under conditions in which it cannot deteriorate. One method of ensuring this is to maintain it at a temperature as close as possible to, but above 0�C.

.
#m%92,-1932 . .'

""T?

`_'

'

Another method is to add a preservative or antiseptic to' the n$& f. instance, pota&m dichromate in the proportion of 1 g per lithe milk,' mpcuric chloride in the proportion. of 1 g per litre of milk, -.@, formal@ in the proportion of 1 to 2 ml per litre of milk ). In the seco@d method, pro&on should be made for the treated milk to have.a dist@lrtive colour to avoid it being mistaken for untreated milk. Moreover, should the additive be highly toxic, the receptacle containing the treated milk should be clearly marked to identify it. 5.3.3 Method Used-Determine the butterfat content of the average sample by the Gerber method ( see IS : 1224-1958* ). Calculate from this, to two decimal places, the mass in kilograms of fat produced during 24 hours.
6. FREQUENCY

OF RECORDING

6.1 A record of the quantity of milk and of butterfat produced in 24 hours The time interval between two should be made at least once a mdnth. successive recordings should be within the following extreme limits: 26 to 34 days, for monthly recording; 18 to 24 days, for three-weekly recording; and 12 to 16 days, for fortnightly recording. 6.2 The same recording intervals should, as a general rule, be maintained throughout the period of lactation or of the operational year. Any departure from this rule should be recorded in the report. 7. DURATION OF CCiNTROL

7.1 Milk recording may. be carried out over the whole of the lactation period, that is, using the lactation period method, or over 365 consecutive days, that is, using the operation year method. 7.1.1 Lactation Period Method criteria: b) the lactation calving; This method is defined by the following

a) the control should be exercised during the whole lactation period; period is taken as beginning on the first day after

c) milk-butterfat control (weighing of milk, sampling for analysis ) should not be carried out before the sixth day after calving;
*Determination bf fai in whole milk, evaporated ( unsweetened skim milk, butter milk, and cream by the Gerber method. ) milk, separated milk,

the lactation period is considered to have ended when the cattle is no longer milked twice a day. In this case, by convention, the date for stopping control' is taken: i) in the case of fortnightly control, as the seventh day; ii) in the case of three-weekly control, as the tenth iii) in the case of monthly control, as the fourteenth after the last normal in. the calculation. recording; the day in question day; and day being included

Lactations mayI however, be calculated for as long as the cattle with over 3 kg of milk daily are milked regularly at least once a day for a period longer than one week. 7.1.2 Oprational Year Method - This method is defined by the following criteria: , a) the control begins at any given date and ends on the day preceding that date in the fallowing ye& b) milk-butterfat control ( weighing of mill;* sampling for analysis) should not be carried out before the sixth `day after calving; c) the lactation period is considered to have ended when the cattle is no longer milked twice a day. In this case, by cbnvention, the date for stopping control is taken: i) in the case of fortnightly control, as the seventh ii) in the case of three-weekly control, as the tenth iii) in the case of monthly control, as the fourteenth after the last normal in the calculation. recording, the day in question day; day; and day being included

Lactation may, however, be calculated for as long as the cattle with over 3 kg of milk daily are milked regularly at least once a day for a period longer than one week. 8. REFERENCE LACTATION PERIOD

8.1 Whichever method is followed, and in ofvier to be able to compare the milking value of cattle, the lactation periads of which are different but exceed 305 days, a period designated as the reference period, corresponding to the first 305 days of lactation, should be taken as the basis of comparison. 8.2 The results of this reference lactation period of 305 days should be provided in addition to those of the lactation period or operational year, for all cattle belonging to any one of the following categories: a) registered cattle; in the grading register; b) cattle entered

cattle which, on account of their descent and the right to be entered in the, herd book register; or cattle which, on account of their descent and the right to be issued with an official pedigree OF RESULTS

9. EXPRESSION

/

9.1 Methods of Calculation - The total quantity of milk and butterfat, as well as the percentage of butterfat in the milk, can be calculated from the data collected during milk recording, in one of the three ways given in the Appendix A. A practical worked out example is given in Appendix B. \ NOTE- Variants of these methods of calculation are permitted, but if any is used, this should be mentioned in the milk recording report. The total masses of milk and of butterfat should be expressed in kilogrammes, the figure being obtained from the calculated value by rounding it to the -whole number immediately above it if the first decimal is 5 or more, otherwise to the wholenumber below. The percentage of butterfat in the milk should be rounded to two decimal places on the same principle. 9.2 Remarks

9.2.1 If, owing to vis major* ( paid holidays for instance ), the recording is suspended for a period not exceeding 60 days, the missing figure or figures may be replaced by the means of the results of the recordings immediately before and aft& it. If the `interruption exceeds 60 days, such averages shall not be recognized; 9.2.2 The results obtained by the methods of calculation given in Appendix A should be registered without any correction or modification whatsoever.

f) Whether the frequency of testing has been changed in the course of the lactation or operational year.
